Guideline: Use Cache Components as the current cache model
Description: Cache Components is the current Next.js 16 cache model and the foundation for use cache, cacheLife, cacheTag, and updateTag.
Do: Enable cacheComponents for routes that should use the new cache model
Don't: Treat the old fetch-only mental model as the primary cache contract

Guideline: Use use cache for cacheable functions and components
Description: The use cache directive marks a route, component, or function as cacheable under Cache Components.
Do: Place use cache at file, component, or function scope where the result is cacheable
Don't: Cache runtime-sensitive data without passing it in as arguments
Code Good:
'use cache'
export default async function Page() { }
Code Bad: export default async function Page() { /* uncached by accident */ }

Description: Use cacheLife with use cache to make cache freshness explicit and readable.
Do: Choose a cacheLife profile that matches update frequency
Don't: Leave cache behavior implicit when the data has a known freshness window

Description: Use cacheTag inside cached scopes to support targeted invalidation.
Do: Assign stable tags to cacheable data
Don't: Use broad invalidation when a specific tag is enough

Description: Use updateTag from Server Actions when the UI must reflect a mutation immediately.
Do: Call updateTag after a successful mutation in a Server Action
Code Bad: revalidateTag('cart') // when immediate refresh is required

Description: The one-argument revalidateTag form is deprecated; profile="max" is the current stale-while-revalidate contract.
Do: Use revalidateTag(tag, "max") for background refresh semantics
Don't: Rely on the deprecated single-argument revalidateTag(tag)
